A man in love with his family, that´s Marcos Rogério Lima, “Pezao” is married and has a 2 years old little girl.

A born athlete, with 12 years old use to joke with his friends at school. “They were afraid of my kick.”

At 14, he passed for the most terrible moment of his life. He stopped playing sports, got away from his family, and got inside the world of drugs. “I use to think of bad thinks and graffiti.” He tells.

Sad and tired to see the life his son was taking, his father argued with him, shook his brothers medals, world champion on judo, in his son’s face. “My father told me this was what my brother were accomplishing for the future and asked me what I was getting in life. It got to me and I decided I needed to do something to get out of the streets.”

That’s how Marcos found boxing. “Boxing is all about my personality, my aggressiveness is big, but boxing doesn’t give you many options so I decided to go to MMA.”

The dream of his father to see him succeed in life, was coming true. The peak was when he got to the TUF house. “This is without a question, the most amazing moment in my life. I want to be here and make my family proud.”
   
Anderson Silva is his biggest idol inside the UFC. “he is awesome. A lot of technique and a good person”  he says.   
When asked if he is afraid of losing, he says: “I’m not afraid of any opponent, I’m afraid of having a bad performance, lose my chance.”

When and why did you start training for fighting? About six years ago, to teach my daughter to protect herself.

What ranks and titles have you held? Golden Gloves boxing champ, NAGA champ, Black Belt in Jiu-Jitsu

Do you have any heroes? Everyday people that take care of their families.

What is your favorite technique? Whatever gets the job done.

What does it mean for you to fight in the WEC? I get a chance to compete against the best.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? No

What was your job before you started fighting? Loss prevention for Wal-Mart

How has your training changed since coming into the WEC? It’s become a way of life doing what I love to do everyday.

What is it like to fight on live TV in the WEC? It’s like a dream

How have the stakes changed now that you’re with the WEC? Every fight is like my last chance.

How has the competition level changed since joining the WEC? It’s like going to college or to the pros.

Most memorable professional fight? My most memorable fight was a boxing match against Tim O'Neil in Madison Square Garden. In the boxing world, few places are more legendary than Madison Square Garden, but to compete and win there was indescribable. 

What was your most challenging professional fight? Definitely my most challenging fight was my very first WEC match which was against Sergio Gomez. My left eye was swollen shut within the first 10 seconds of the fight and I continued for two rounds. My will and heart was tested, but in the end my composure kept me calm and focused to secure a guillotine submission.

Did you compete in any other sport at college or professional level? I received offers for football from a few colleges, but my focus at the time was on my family and taking care of my daughter especially. My interest in combat sports was specifically to help teach my daughter to protect herself, but success in competition has given the means to provide for her as well.

Who were your training partners for this fight? This fight I was able to train with Paul Buentello, Pete Spratt, Rodrigo Pinheiro and the team at XFC Training Center in Austin, Texas. As always, my team sparring partner is Albert Martinez.

Did you put more emphasis towards a fighting style or adjust your training to prepare for your opponent? Training for this fight was no different than for any in the past. In my camp, we don't focus on a specific game-plan unique to each opponent. 

What is your favorite thing about this sport? The equal combination in mental and physical aspects involved to compete at this level. Most people only see the physical aspect of the sport, but few truly understand the mental component needed to be successful. It may appear to be just a brawl, but a 'human-chess match' is a more accurate description.

How long do you see yourself staying in this sport? Longevity plays an important role in my training. I put an equal amount of time into the care for my joints and body as I do into sparring and drills.  My camp and I have a plan which should allow me to compete for another 10 years and still be able to keep up with grandchildren long after my career.

A product of North Carolina, Marcus Jones enters the house with an impressive athletic pedigree.  A three-sport star at Southwest Onslow High School, Jones earned several accolades including Gatorade All-American for football, All-Conference for basketball and was a two-time state champ in discus.

Jones elected to stay in state and enrolled at the University of North Carolina where he became a standout defensive end for the Tar Heels.  An elite pass rusher, Jones was a four-time letterman, an All-American and the 1995 ACC Defensive Player of the Year during his UNC career. 

In 1996, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers chose Jones with the 22nd pick in the NFL draft.  During his eight seasons he totaled 24 career sacks, including 13 during the 2000 season, placing him eighth in the league.  After six seasons with the Bucs, Jones moved over to the Buffalo Bills where injuries forced him out of the league.

A life-long fan of mixed martial arts, Jones turned to the sport following retirement and began training with the renowned team Gracie Tampa and former “The Ultimate Fighter” alums Brandon Sene, Shame Primm and Matt Arroyo.  A natural athlete with powerful hands, the 35-year-old Jones is looking to improve his overall game while in the house.

When and why did you start training for fighting? 2005, I started with kickboxing, and a year later I started training in MMA. I love competition, individual sports, and testing myself against someone who wants to hurt you. I was 13 when I started training, and I haven't even had a year off. Sport is an important part of my life.

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? Amateur mma record 20-3, Two Polish amateur championships, four tournament wins in multi-fighters brackets.

Any belts/ranks in grappling disciplines? BJJ Black Belt since 2019, So far I have won over 50 Polish tournaments, but the five most important titles are, of course, in black belts:

  • Polish Gi Championship 
  • Polish No-Gi Championship 
  • Polish Adcc pro 
  • Ireland Adcc pro 
  • European Championship CBJJ

Any belts/ranks in striking disciplines? No, I’m ground beast ;) I can't striking ;p 

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? Ibjjf European Championship Black Belts (Madrid, Spain) Tournament Final vs Catriel Fernandes Rodrigues from Brazil. Before this fight, I was on a very long winning streak, and for a moment, I felt immortal. It was a mistake, because I lost the final by sub, and I realized that this defeat was more beneficial to me than the victory.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Jon Jones. UFC Mount Rushmore. An elite fighter who is one of the most versatile in the history of the sport. Jon is also a battle with his own demons. The entire world watched his subsequent falls, and he always came back. He has the mind of a champion, but many fans downplay his legacy due to his personal issues. Villians and superhero in one person. Real life Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde. 

Did you go to college and if so, what degree did you earn? I graduated from the University of Gdańsk. I am a mechatronics engineer and have a master's degree in physical education.

What was your job before you started fighting? I've been fight since I was 13. Work has always been a sideline to sport :) I run my own gym and help out with my wife's events company. In the past, I've been a security guard, a professional driver, and a school teacher. :) During my studies, I worked various jobs to earn money for college.

Origin of nickname: My longtime manager came up with this nickname, and I liked it. I'm big, I like to dominate my opponents and finish fights quickly, like Godzilla finish city buildings and other monsters. It's also a play on words with my surname. I don't know if I resemble the giant reptile, but the Godzilla theme will also be used in my entrance song.

Personal Life / Background (family stuff, kids, etc.): Wife Justina, son Antoni. I'm the co-owner and founder of Dragon Den Grappler Ełk. The biggest MMA/BJJ gym in the Masurian region. We currently have over 400 members. My "students" compete in Polish championships, but also in professional fights where I am often part of the corner.

Who are 3 people you'd love to meet or work with (celebrities, content creators, other fighters, sports stars)? Gordon Ryan, Jon Jones, Jason Statham 

What are your hobbies, activities or other interests when not training for a fight? BJJ is my biggest hobby, next to MMA. I'm trying to raise my son to be a good and righteous person, and from an early age I've been teaching him that sport and training are important in life, because discipline teaches determination. Other hobbies? Cars, movies, console games, and emptying the fridge ;)

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training kickboxing when I was 17 years old, and I fell in love with combat sports from the very beginning. In 2020, I made the transition to MMA, and I’ve been fully committed to the sport ever since.

What does it mean for you to fight for the UFC? It’s the realization of my dream.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Valentina Shevchenko. I’ve been following her since her kickboxing days. I admire the way she has dedicated her life to this sport, and despite all of her success, she still manages to make time for her family and friends. She has found the perfect balance, and that’s something I truly respect.

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? I don’t have any heroes. My faith in God is all I need.

What are your current ranks in martial arts? Blue Belt in BJJ

Specific accomplishments in pro competition: WKN International Kickboxing Champion, K-1 Grand Prix winner, and Balkan Kickboxing Champion.

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why? The second-to-last fight of my career, where I suffered my first professional loss, was the most important one. It taught me a lot, and I came back from that defeat as a stronger person. I made key changes in my life, and they helped me grow both as an athlete and as a person.

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? I want to inspire children—especially girls and women—to believe in themselves and pursue their dreams.

Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you? I want to leave a lasting legacy in this sport and make the world a better place than I found it. I want children to look up to me, and one day, I hope to help them build a better life through sports, just as I have.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I graduated from high school and earned a college degree in physical therapy.

What was your job before you started fighting? When I was younger, I worked as a massage therapist so I could afford my training. Later, I started coaching children. Three years ago, I opened my own gym, which I now run together with my boyfriend, called “Striker Team.”

Favorite grappling technique: Arm triangle choke.

Favorite striking technique: Left uppercut to the body.

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: I enjoy coaching at my gym and spending time with my boyfriend and my closest friends. I also love being an aunt and spending time with my nephews. I love the ocean, reading books, eating good food, and traveling after my fights and victories.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training in 2011. I took my first fight and fell in love with the sport and all the martial arts.

Who are your main training partners? Jose Delgado, Greg Foster, Moses Diaz and UFC bantamweight Kyler Phillips.

What ranks and titles have you held? Black belt in Jiu-Jitsu (earned in 2022)

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It means my dreams are coming true, with hard work and dedication. It’s everything. I can now train full-time. 

What do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why? I always look back at my second UFC fight against Jin Soo Son. Both of us coming off debut losses against Petr Yan and me against Cory Sandhagen. I went into that fight knowing another loss could mean getting cut from the UFC and he knew that too, which made for an amazing fight and we got a Fight of the Night bonus. I wanted it more and got my hand raised and I knew I belonged.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? My favorite fighter would have to be Demetrius Johnson. I think he just embodies what it means to be a mixed martial artist. He’s not a one-trick pony and can do it all and is one of the greatest champions.

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? My heroes outside of fighting would have to be my father, Mario Sr., and uncle Francisco. To me they are the best examples of true hard workers and the best of family men and are always there for me when I need help navigating life.

Beyond championship of money, what motivates you? Just to be a version of yourself every day and always riding that edge. Always chasing your limits and finding out who you truly are.

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? Just the life of Mario. I just hope people take inspiration from it in whatever they do, andrealize that if you’re consistent in chasing a dream it’ll come true.

What was your job before you started fighting? Auto glass installer

Favorite grappling technique: Guillotine

Favorite Striking technique: Flying knee 

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: My wife Ashley has been amazing this whole career and has been with me since the beginning. We have a daughter, Adelina; she is my biggest fan and is an amazing little girl with a beautiful soul. We have a dachshund too; he’s a fun lil dog always wanting to play and tear things up. It’s a nice little family. I’m always jumping between hobbies but this year my goals are to become more fluent in Spanish to maybe open some opportunities and also want to get into motorcycle riding this year.

What is one thing you want UFC fans around the world to know about you? If fighting didn’t exist I would’ve pursued being some kind of competitive driver/mechanic or become Steve Irwin himself.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started early, at about 7-8 years old. I watched a lot of action movies, such as Resident Evil, 13th District, and I was impressed by characters, especially female characters, who could defend themselves well. Also, I started training because I wanted to defend myself in real life, because I was bullied a lot in the neighborhood and at school (especially at school).

Training: I wake up in the second half of the day, and train in the evening, then go home and spend the whole night playing Skyrim (The Elder Scrolls)

What professional titles have you held? Belt Heroine FC

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? WMMMA World Champion, champion of Kazakhstan 

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines? Blue belt in BJJ

Any belts / ranks in striking disciplines? Boxing champion of Kazakhstan 2 times

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? For me, it was a very difficult fight with Gillian Robinson.  I fought without an ACL in my knee, and throughout my entire fight camp I worked as security at a club on the night shift. Due to the tough fight camp, I felt very tired during fight week. It was very difficult.

TRAINING: I get up at 4am and head to the gym for cardio or strength training. Afterwards I go back home and get ready for work. I work at Peoples Natural Gas. After work, I head to my gym and get my second workout in. The day will determine what I'll be working on. I try to leave no stone unturned. I get a good mix of MMA training, BJJ (Gi & NoGi), wrestling, boxing & Muay Thai. After my sessions, I head home and spend the rest of my night with my wife & daughter.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started back in 2007. I had wanted to start training for a while, but here in Pittsburgh there weren’t many places to train back then. By chance, I ran into a neighbor who was carrying a duffle bag with his gear. I asked him what he did and he told me he trained MMA. He offered to train me a little and a month later sent me to a local pro fighter who trained me for my first eight amateur fights. I was hooked after the first practice and decided to forego Culinary Arts school and just focus on training and fighting.

What ranks and titles have you held? PinnacleFC Professional Featherweight Champ, Gladiators of the Cage Professional Champ, Brawlroom MMA Amateur Featherweight Champ, Rocktagon Amateur Featherweight Champ, Cage of Chaos Amateur Featherweight Champ & 2011 NAAFS National Amateur Featherweight Champ

Do you have any heroes? My mom for raising three kids by herself after my father passed away from cancer. Also, my wife. The way she juggles working as a nurse, being a mom, a wife and just being the glue that keeps everything together is simply amazing. She is always pushing me and supporting me and my fighting career.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It means that I've achieved a goal I set for myself almost 10 years ago. It's my chance to show the world that just because we don't have a big name gym in our area that we still put out some great fighters. I want to put Western PA on the map. It also means that I have an opportunity to test my skills against the best in the world for the best organization in the world. Also, I'll get verified on Twitter & take more vacations to Disney World with my wife & daughter. 

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I did some community college but never earned a degree.

What was your job before you started fighting? I was actually set to start Culinary Arts school prior to starting MMA.  But I fell in love with the sport & decided to focus on that over going to school.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I was undefeated as an amateur with a 9-0 record and 9 finishes. I also won a national amateur MMA title in 2011.

Ranks in any martial arts styles: Brown Belt in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu

Favorite grappling technique: S Mount Armbar

Favorite Striking technique: Check Hook

When and why did you start training for fighting? I’ve wanted to be a professional fighter for as long as I can remember. I started wrestling as a teenager, and once my wrestling career ended, I went straight into MMA training under Duke Roufus at Roufusport in Milwaukee. It was a natural transition. I knew this was what I was meant to do. 

What professional titles have you held? I am a 2x APFC lightweight champion. 

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? 3x NCAA All American 

Any belts/ranks in grappling disciplines? Blue belt in jiu-jitsu  

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? I don’t think I’ve ever been in a fight that wasn’t tough. Every opponent brings a different challenge, and each fight has pushed me to grow in some way. Even going back to my wrestling days, every match has taught me something physically, mentally, or emotionally. That’s what makes this sport so powerful. 

Who is your favorite fighter and why? GSP has always been my favorite fighter. He was one of the first guys I watched growing up, and I was drawn to his style and how composed he stayed under pressure. He’s a true martial artist. Well-rounded, disciplined, and respectful, and he represents everything great about this sport. I see a lot of myself in that approach. 

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I attended the University of Wisconsin–Oshkosh, but I didn’t graduate due to the impact of COVID. When everything shut down, I took it as a sign to fully commit to MMA. I made the decision to leave school and dedicate myself completely to pursuing a professional fighting career 

What was your job before you started fighting? I had many odd jobs, mostly in different fields of construction. 

Origin of nickname: I got my nickname back in high school on the wrestling mats. I had a relentless, aggressive style, and people started calling me 'Shark.' 

Personal Life / Background: I’m not married and don’t have kids. Right now, my entire focus is on my career — I’ve dedicated my life to mixed martial arts. Everything I do, day in and day out, revolves around becoming the best fighter I can be. 

Who are 3 people you'd love to meet or work with? I’ve never really been starstruck or into celebrity culture, but if I had to pick a few people to meet, it would be OGs of the fight game — legends like GSP, Jon Jones, and Chuck Liddell. I’d love the chance to pick their brains and learn from their experience at the highest level. 

What are your hobbies, activities or other interests when not training for a fight? At this point in my life, all my hobbies are in mixed martial arts… eat, sleep, train.

I have a giant shark tattooed on my chest that represents my fighting spirit. It’s a symbol of how I approach competition: aggressive, relentless, and always moving forward.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? GSP has always been my favorite fighter. He was one of the first guys I watched growing up, and I was drawn to his style and how composed he stayed under pressure. He’s a true martial artist. Well-rounded, disciplined, and respectful, and he represents everything great about this sport. I see a lot of myself in that approach. 

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I attended the University of Wisconsin–Oshkosh, but I didn’t graduate due to the impact of COVID. When everything shut down, I took it as a sign to fully commit to MMA. I made the decision to leave school and dedicate myself completely to pursuing a professional fighting career 

What was your job before you started fighting? I had many odd jobs, mostly in different fields of construction. 

Origin of nickname: I got my nickname back in high school on the wrestling mats. I had a relentless, aggressive style, and people started calling me 'Shark.' 

Personal Life / Background: I’m not married and don’t have kids. Right now, my entire focus is on my career — I’ve dedicated my life to mixed martial arts. Everything I do, day in and day out, revolves around becoming the best fighter I can be. 

Who are 3 people you'd love to meet or work with? I’ve never really been starstruck or into celebrity culture, but if I had to pick a few people to meet, it would be OGs of the fight game — legends like GSP, Jon Jones, and Chuck Liddell. I’d love the chance to pick their brains and learn from their experience at the highest level. 

What are your hobbies, activities or other interests when not training for a fight? At this point in my life, all my hobbies are in mixed martial arts… eat, sleep, train.

I have a giant shark tattooed on my chest that represents my fighting spirit. It’s a symbol of how I approach competition: aggressive, relentless, and always moving forward.
